Fox News’ lone liberal host clapped back at President Donald Trump’s frequent criticism of her, asking, “Why is this man not busier?”

The 80-year-old Fox fanatic has often shared his opinions of the network online, especially of its outspoken left-leaning host Jessica Tarlov, who he called “one of the worst ‘personalities’ on television” in April — as well as “a real loser” in July.

Trump has also called Tarlov “one of the Least Attractive and Talented People on all of Television.”

Tarlov, 42, addressed his frequent criticism on the podcast Pod Save America, saying, “Why is this man not busier? There are better things to do.”

“If I had a son I would definitely teach him that when you grow up you should write about how a woman looks on television and sounds, and then call her ‘a big dummy,’” Tarlov retorted.

Left-leaning Fox News host Jessica Tarlov questioned why President Trump isn’t ‘busier’ in response to his frequent criticisms of her ( Getty )

Tarlov was on the podcast promoting her book, I Disagree: Winning Arguments Without Losing Friends, which hit bookstores on Tuesday. The book, which is a mesh between memoir and advice, details how she handles that type of criticism.

“By the president coming after me and looking at the content of the criticism, I actually got to a place where I genuinely feel like when people pick on you because of style, that you’ve just done really well on substance,” she said.

“That feels good, the inner monologue feels good. It’s still sad and crazy,” she added.

Tarlov, who joined Fox News as a commentator in 2017, is known as the primary liberal voice on the network's “The Five.” She recently signed a three-year contract with the network — despite Trump’s suggestion that the show would be better off without her.

“I’m trying to show that a Democratic voice like mine can exist there, without an apology,” she told the Los Angeles Times about her Fox position. “And that a person with strong liberal beliefs can bring that same perspective to a host of outlets and places.”

When asked about Trump trying to get her fired, she recently told The Guardian, “I think that [Fox CEO} Suzanne Scott and the entire leadership team know exactly who I am, and that they want me to keep doing what I’m doing.”

She continued: “And if it aggravates him – he would just get annoyed at somebody else, anyone. If he’s in a bad mood, he’s in a bad mood. And I think he understands that as well.”

“I’ve never had a conversation with him, but the idea of posting ‘Dear Fox executives, fire Jessica Tarlov’ or calling into The Five and saying the show would be better without her, I don’t think he thinks that means that I’m going to get fired from my job. … But yes, in general, we don’t respond to it, and there’s no reason to, and honestly it just makes it worse.”

A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon in the Texas' capital of Austin, local officials said.

The man was in serious but stable condition at a hospital after being shot once in the torso on Austin’s north side, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis said at a news conference with the city's mayor and other officials present.

The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, didn’t immediately respond to requests for details.

Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, Davis told reporters.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson said he wants the city's police department to be involved in the investigation so it can provide “clear, third-party eyes” in the process. Watson said he does not think it would be appropriate for ICE to conduct the investigation on its own.

Davis said there were not many facts she could provide so soon after the shooting, but added the department’s special investigation unit was at the scene.

A dark blue Toyota Corolla was parked under an overpass with damage to its passenger-side door and what appeared to be bullet holes, local media reported.

A large law enforcement presence was at the scene, along with a crowd of onlookers.

U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, a Democrat representing parts of Austin, called for transparency as the shooting is investigated.

“The horror has come to our city: ICE has shot a person in Austin this morning,” Casar wrote on X. “As the facts emerge, I am demanding a full, independent investigation, immediate release of the body camera footage, and accountability for any ICE officer who broke the law.”

In July, an ICE officer fatally shot 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, of Houston, after federal agents driving unmarked vehicles pursued him while he was taking his construction crew to a job site.

Also in July, 25-year-old Johan Sebastián, a Colombian man, was shot by an ICE officer in Maine. The officer is an Army veteran who has struggled with serious mental health issues since early childhood and never should have been given a badge and gun to patrol American streets, several of his close relatives told The Associated Press.

The shootings come amid a Trump administration push to carry out its mass deportations agenda. While the administration is no longer cracking down on individual cities, arrests are still occurring.

The administration’s enforcement efforts were widely condemned last winter after the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minnesota.

A one-year-old boy was taken to hospital with facial injuries after a dog bit his face while he sat in a pushchair, police have said.

The dog, believed to be a German Shepherd, is alleged to have lunged towards the boy on Shirley Precinct, a local shopping centre, in Southampton, at around 3:20pm on 21 August.

The one-year-old suffered two small puncture wounds and grazing to his face, Hampshire and Isle of White Constabulary said.

Police have now shared an image of a woman they want to speak with in connection with the incident.

The woman is described by police as white, 5ft 7ins tall, and of large build

open image in gallery The woman was seen with a large dog believed to be a German Shepherd ( Southampton Police )

The dog, wearing a mesh-style muzzle, is believed to be a German Shepherd.

“Since this was reported to us, officers have been carrying out enquiries and are working to establish the exact circumstances surrounding the incident,” police said.

“We are hoping to speak with a woman (pictured) who may have information which could help with our enquiries.”

Last month, a man appeared in court accused of manslaughter after his German Shepherd fatally bit a man on a footpath in Wakefield following an argument about “right of way”.

Emergency services were called to reports of an altercation on the old train line footpath off Blacker Lane in the Calder Grove area on Saturday 15 August.

James Judge, 55, was bitten by a dog and taken to hospital in a critical condition but died shortly after 7pm. His family is being supported by specially trained officers.

Lee Ellis, 55, has been charged with manslaughter and being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control, causing injury resulting in death.

Specialist courtrooms to deal with rape and serious sexual offences are set to be rolled out in a bid to tackle “shamefully low” prosecution rates, Andy Burnham has announced.

Under new government plans, every Crown Court in England and Wales will have at least one courtroom especially set up to hear such cases over the next two years.

Survivors will be offered private entrances and waiting rooms in courts, as well as access to facilities equipped to pre-record evidence and observe sentencing remotely.

All court staff will also receive trauma-informed training, with a single person of contact assigned to each survivor.

The measures, which Rape Crisis England & Wales say are “necessary and long overdue”, are expected to cost around £23 million from the Ministry of Justice budget.

From October, trials will be prioritised with fixed dates rather than placed on floating lists in what the prime minister described as an effort to “rebalance the scales of justice and put victims first.”

Mr Burnham said the plans are “long overdue”, as he acknowledged those who have been “let down” by the justice system.

“Prosecution rates for rape remain shamefully low, with many victims waiting years for justice,” he said

open image in gallery Trials will be prioritised in courts, being given a fixed date rather than being place on “floating lists”, which often leave survivors facing long delays ( PA Archive )

“This is not good enough. That’s why we are making major changes to rebalance the scales of justice and put victims first. This includes rolling out specialist courtrooms for rape and serious sex offences.

“These changes are long overdue and will make a significant difference, but focusing on prosecution alone will not be enough. So as well as ensuring victims get justice, we will step up action to prevent these horrific crimes from happening in the first place.”

In its announcement, the Government credited Labour MP Charlotte Nichols’ “immense strength and bravery” in speaking publicly about being raped and calling for changes to a backlogged system.

In March, Ms Nichols waived her automatic right to anonymity in a powerful Commons speech during which she lamented having to wait more than 1,000 days to go to court

Ciara Bergman, CEO of Rape Crisis England & Wales said: “We’re particularly pleased to see measures that will improve trial efficiency and ensure survivors are better able to participate in, and observe, proceedings.

“The recognition that suitable separate waiting areas, entrances and exits are essential to prevent survivors from being intimidated and distressed by the presence of perpetrators and their supporters is also significant. This welcome change is both necessary and long overdue.”

Lord chancellor Alex Norris acknowledged victims have felt “left alone facing the criminal justice system for too long”.

open image in gallery Prime minister Andy Burnham said the plans are ‘long overdue’ ( PA Wire )

“They have been treated as cases to process and not as people to support,” he said.

“The funding we are announcing today will provide that support that victims deserve – delivering courtrooms that are designed with victim needs in mind and providing specialist training for staff to handle these cases with care.

“Real action to improve our courts. Real action for victims. Real action to deliver the justice they deserve.”

Tory shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy also described the move to tackle delays is “long overdue”, but criticised the government’s decision to restrict jury trials.

“The fact that victims have been withdrawing their cases because they have taken too long has been a disgrace,” he said.

“However, rape trial delays have been used by Labour as their main justification for their attack on juries. If resources can be found to accelerate rape trials, why are they persisting in their attack on this ancient right to jury trials?

“Labour need to get courts sitting throughout the year, end the delays and clear the backlog - not undermine our right to a trial by jury.”

News.title: Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change
News.content:
But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.

He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

News.title: Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool
News.content:
It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: An A to Z guide to what’s in your laundry detergent
News.content:
Laundry is one of those jobs that most of us do on autopilot. Throw a load of washing and your favourite detergent into the drum and wait for the machine to work its magic. Perhaps you’ve never even thought to ask yourself what chemicals you’re putting in with your clothes.

In the UK, detergent brands are legally required to state the use of surfactants and enzymes (the main ingredients for stain removal) in a way that is easy to understand, but you may see additional compounds that leave you scratching your head.

Here, I break down the words on the back of the bottle to help you understand exactly what you’re putting in your washing. Given that I’ve just tested 26 laundry detergents and developed an app to help you clean your clothes better, I’m the best woman for the job.

Below, you’ll find the most common detergent ingredients listed A to Z. If you’ve got a burning question about a laundry buzzword, I should be able to help. Add any in the comments section below.

Anionic

There are two main types of surfactants: anionic and non-ionic. A surfactant has a hydrophilic head that loves water and a hydrophobic tail that hates it. Anionic surfactants have a negative charge on their head, which is what helps lift soils and stains from the fabric, though they’re not so good at getting rid of oils. They create a lot of foam but their effectiveness can be limited by minerals found in hard water, which is why they are paired with non-ionic surfactants.

Bio

Short for biological, this label means that a detergent contains enzymes. These are proteins that break down fats, starches and grease, so use bio formulations when you need to tackle stubborn food stains. They are effective at lower temperatures but they can be abrasive on sensitive skin. If your skin is easily irritated, opt for non-bio, instead.

News.title: Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash
News.content:
Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak brought to end in Canada draw
News.content:
The record books will show that this meeting, a proper Test full of ebbs and flows, was neither. And, no matter the pre-match belief of England head coach John Mitchell, Canada are not on the same level of professionalism and funding as his side. Mitchell had brought back nine players, many of whom featured in last year’s World Cup final victory, after the thrashing of Australia last week with the expectation that the history of 2025 would repeat itself. Canada had other ideas.

“The plan on the field at the last scrum was to go for the win,” Canada captain Sophie de Goede said. “And then the message came on from the sideline to kick it out. In that moment you have to trust your coach and your coaching staff, and we’ll have a discussion about it later. If we had given away a penalty off the next breakdown, we’d be sitting here going, ‘Why didn’t you kick it out?’”

England’s downfall came at the set-piece, where their line-out malfunctioned and their scrum never gained dominance, in a tale which was not too dissimilar to last week. The hosts came second in the physical battle, too, which was uncharacteristic of them; losing Hannah Botterman to a shoulder injury did not help, either. All told, Canada just looked as though they wanted it a little bit more and maybe this was the wake-up call the Red Roses needed: when you are at the top, and at the top by a margin, every team want to be the one to dethrone you.

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
Doctors in Frankfurt have been summoned for an urgent public health briefing after a third person died of malaria this week in the German city.

At least eight people have been infected with malaria in Frankfurt since July, when health officials suspect mosquitoes were brought into the country aboard an aeroplane, before biting multiple people and infecting them in and around the city’s airport.

Six of the cases, reported in July and August, have been amongst airport workers, two of whom died earlier in the summer.

But on Monday this week, two people living in the Schwanheim district, a neighbourhood close to the airport of around 20,000 people, were reported to have been infected with malaria – one of whom died on Thursday.

“We contacted all the GPs in Schwanheim directly earlier this week, as well as all the medical doctors from emergency departments and ambulance services and informed them about the current situation so that everybody is aware,” Dr Peter Tinnemann, Director of the Public Health Department for the city of Frankfurt, told The Telegraph.

Hall said: “I was obviously supporting all of them with Dan [Burn] being there, Elliot [Anderson], Anthony [Gordon], and big Tino [Livramento].

Hall produced another stellar display to help keep Hull at bay. Manager Matthias Jaissle, who went viral after the game for buying a Toon fan’s birthday meal after bumping into the party at a city restaurant, cannot wait to see what more the player can contribute to his team.

MANCHESTER UNITED players ran over SIX KILOMETRES less than their Fulham counterparts on Sunday.

Red Devils boss Michael Carrick insisted there was nothing wrong with the urgency and effort from his players in the 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage.



But club legend Gary Neville called United a “genuine disgrace“.

And the statistics back up the Sky Sports pundit rather than the man in the Old Trafford hot seat.



According to data collected by FotMob, United players collectively covered 110.2km – a full 6.5km less than Fulham‘s 116.7km.

Look into the other running metrics and it becomes even more worrying for Carrick.

Carrick could have been under serious pressure had Matheus Cunha not salvaged a draw with his deflected 89th-minute strike.

But he is by no means out of the woods after a flat performance and dropped points against a side who have not won in the Premier League all season.

Carrick now has an extended international break to ponder his next move.

Sports.title: Mo Salah banned from driving for six months after ace caught speeding in £400k Rolls two days after he quit Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTIE ace Mo Salah has been banned from driving after his £400,000 Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding.

The Egyptian forward failed to tell police who was behind the wheel of the electric Spectre when it was caught by a mobile camera in March.



It happened in Wilmslow, Cheshire, two days after he had dramatically announced he would be leaving Liverpool at the end of last season.

Salah, 34, the Premier League’s all-time top foreign scorer, did not respond to two court summonses sent to his £4million mansion.



He was convicted in his absence by magistrates in Warrington, Cheshire, last month of failing to identify the driver under the Single Justice Procedure.

A charge of exceeding the 30mph speed limit was withdrawn.

The Kop legend, who now plays for Turkish side Trabzonspor, was handed a six-month driving ban and £660 fine. He was also ordered to pay £120 in court costs and a victim surcharge of £264.

In 2022, Salah was clocked in his Ferrari F8 Tributo doing 63mph in a 50mph zone in Stockport. He got a £200 fine and three penalty points.

And he was filmed apparently using his mobile phone behind the wheel close to Anfield in 2018.

He was not prosecuted after police said there was “insufficient evidence”.

FURIOUS Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa faces an FA sanction after claiming officials “refused to let Manchester United lose” during their 1–1 draw.

Matheus Cunha‘s deflected 89th minute strike rescued a draw at Craven Cottage and delayed a full-blown crisis in the away dugout.



But Arbeloa, who replaced Marco Silva in the summer and is bookies favourite alongside Michael Carrick to be the first manager to be sacked, accused officials of being influenced by their apology to United after the Manchester derby injustice.

Arbeloa was vexed that United received a free-kick for a foul on Harry Maguire 35 seconds before Cunha’s equaliser denied Fulham a first win of the season after five matches.



The Spaniard raged: “Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they would not let Man Utd lose. We deserved a little bit more.”

“We were so, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.



“We knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referee has been doing in all the matches, so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky.”

Arbeloa felt the free-kick for Cesar Palacios’ foul on Maguire was soft and claimed ref Michael Oliver gave “all fouls” to United – because of the “error in judgement” by the officials who incorrectly awarded Erling Haaland‘s winner at Old Trafford last weekend.

In his later press conference, Arbeloa appeared to row back on his comments a tad – but still said he “was not really happy”.

He added: “My English is not so good. Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.”

Sports.content:

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has plenty to ponder over the international break (Image: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/Shutterstock)

How the mighty have fallen.

‌



Manchester United used to win games in Fergie time. Now they are left to snatch a lucky draw from the jaws of defeat.

‌



It spared them some embarrassment - but not much. Five games into the Premier League campaign, United are already 10 points behind Manchester City and another season is in danger of flatlining.

‌



United were so poor at times that Sky co-commentator Gary Neville called the performance “absolutely pathetic” and added: “I've watched United since the age of five. That's the worst 15 minutes I've seen them play.”

That might seem over the top. But let’s not forget that Neville is a club legend, former teammate of United boss Michael Carrick and his comments hit hard. They will resonate.

They are also in keeping with a mood at a club which demands and expects better. The fans even turned on Carrick in the way they booed the substitution of Kobbie Mainoo at a time when they were chasing an equaliser.

Eventually, they got the leveller courtesy of Matheus Cunha’s deflected shot which was in keeping with their performance. It came after a big stroke of luck which was barely deserved.

‌



The goal at the other end which had put Fulham ahead came after Lisandro Martinez put through his own goal in real Keystone Cops fashion. It was laughably bad.

United desperately needed a win to lift the spirits and change the mood around Carrick going into a three-week international break. That will now feel painfully long.

View 3 Images Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike rescued a point for Manchester United at Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Sir Alex Ferguson was looking on from the posh seats and he must be wondering what on earth has gone wrong with United’s latest experiment.

Doesn’t this sound all too familiar? Club legend comes in to give United a lift, gets the desired effect and then - surprise, surprise - the next season is much harder to manage. This time it is Carrick and before it was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

It is happening again. And then, in the background, you have got joint United owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe making a fool of himself again.

‌



It was Ratcliffe making damning remarks about the country being “on the slide” in an interview about the Government failing businesses.

Honestly, for such an intelligent man his lack of self awareness is incredible. Talk about timing. You might want to get your own affairs in order first, Sir Jim. What a plonker.

But that is what United have come to. They spend millions, buy without much of a plan and leave themselves with a creaking defence marshalled by Harry Maguire who, at 33, showed his age as he lost his balance and crashed into a crate of bottles on the touchline.

‌



View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez put through his own goal to put Fulham ahead (Image: Getty Images)

Chasing after Fulham’s Josh King and Alex Iwobi must take it out of you. Fulham deserved more than a draw and the result at least takes them off the bottom and leaves Tottenham rock bottom going into the international break.

And that is the point. United’s first five fixtures - Hull, Ipswich, Everton, Manchester City and Fulham - was quite a friendly start. And they have blown it.

‌



Yes, they did OK first half as Bruno Fernandes hit the post and Cunha’s looping effort also hit the woodwork. But Fulham were good and are improving under Alvaro Arbeloa.

Fulham were the better team from the start of the second half. The opening goal came after 63 minutes. Calvin Bassey intercepted Mainoo’s loose pass, strode forward and his shot was parried by Senne Lammens only for Martinez to deflect the rebound into his own net.

Finally United showed some heart. They pushed forward in the closing stages and nicked a point in the last minute. Typical United. Cunha’s shot deflected off David Affengruber for an equaliser.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola launches Florian Wirtz defence after stinging Jamie Carragher criticism
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola launches Florian Wirtz defence after stinging Jamie Carragher criticism

Jamie Carragher was critical of Florian Wirtz's performance against Bournemouth, but Andoni Iraola reckons that he made the difference for Liverpool in the second half

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola was left pleased with Florian Wirtz (Image: aspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola has praised Florian Wirtz for his second-half turnaround which helped Liverpool beat Bournemouth 1-0. The Reds claimed all three points at the Vitality Stadium, with Alexander Isak scoring the decisive goal.

‌



But it wasn't going Liverpool's way in the first half, with Wirtz in particular struggling to have a positive impact on the game. That was when Jamie Carragher singled out the £116million signing, saying: "Wirtz has been really poor again. It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all.

‌



"In the main, people have been understanding of his situation. He's new to the league and Liverpool were poor last season. When you come for that price tag, people want goals and assists."

‌



In the second period, the 23-year-old was more lively and played a part in Isak's goal, drawing James Hill out to give his team-mate space to finish. But when Wirtz was subbed off in the 73rd minute, Carragher brutally said that he could have 'no complaints'.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Iraola, though, believes that the German ultimately helped Liverpool win the match, telling Sky Sports: "He started the game slowly, I agree. The first minute they went quite intense and we were not quite with us.

"The duels in the middle. After that first phase, I think we improved. Florian has helped us also to improve.

"Second half he was playing much better, he was finding better spots to receive and turn. Probably we haven't found the last part or moment to score but I think I'm much more happy with his second half than his first one."

‌



Should Andoni Iraola drop Florian Wirtz? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz was criticised by Jamie Carragher against Bournemouth (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Iraola added: "I'm obviously happy with the result. I know it's a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points.

‌



"We could see in the game, at the beginning in the first 20 minutes, we weren't at the level at the game, and it has cost us until afterwards, where we finished the first half better.

"The second half we played better. But that beginning of the game kind of - not surprised us because we knew where we were coming to - but it was difficult for us.

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher branded Florian Wirtz 'really poor' in the first half (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Article continues below

"We could see a bit later when Bournemouth started to get tired that in the second half we controlled the game much better. We even had chances to finish but didn't score the second one. But that first part of the game, we were not winning duels, second balls and when they play with this intensity, you have to be at their level."

Sports.title: Gary Neville slams worst Man Utd display EVER after Fulham goal - 'Absolutely pathetic'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville slams worst Man Utd display EVER after Fulham goal - 'Absolutely pathetic'

Gary Neville was left astounded by the way Manchester United conceded against the Cottager and the ex-defender did not hold back on his thoughts

View 2 Images Gary Neville launched a stinging criticism of Manchester United (Image: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/Shutterstock)

Gary Neville labelled Manchester United's start to the second half as "the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen" the club play. Fulham took the lead after half time in a goal strewn with errors by the Reds.

‌



It began with Matheus Cunha being easily dispossessed by Calvin Bassey, who drove forward with the ball and forced a save out of Senne Lammens. The Reds goalkeeper was then caught in two minds after Lisandro Martinez tapped the ball back to him.

‌



He seemingly could not decide whether to save the ball with his foot or with his hand and by the time he made up his mind, the ball was already in. After the goal was conceded, Neville tore into his former side while commentating for Sky Sports.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He said: “I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen them play. Absolutely pathetic. They have walked for 15 minutes and you get what you deserve in a football match.”

When the camera panned to Michael Carrick, Neville added: "Maybe there will be a reaction but I've never seen a lack of effort for 15-20 minutes like I have just seen there. What must he be thinking? He probably cannot believe what he has watched in that last 15 or 20 minutes. He's got to act now."

‌



Neville most likely saw the goal coming as he was anything but impressed with how United started the second half. Before Martinez prodded the ball into his own net, Neville said: "It's a few minutes of the blue mannequins playing against the white mannequins and then it switches around, bizarre football match.

"They won't go anywhere with a lack of urgency like this. I don't know if it's fear, lack of complacency, they're just not working hard."

View 2 Images Martinez's own goal came after some poor United defend (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



United did manage to get an equaliser through Matheus Cunha as the game headed towards the 90-minute mark. The Brazilian struck the ball from just outside the box and watched his effort deflect off David Affengruber and trickle past the wrong-footed Bernd Leno.

His fortuitous goal rescued the Reds from a third consecutive loss in all competitions. Carrick's side came into the match having lost to Manchester City last week and 3-2 to Brighton and Hove Albion in the League Cup.

After the match, former United ace Ashley Young tore into United, saying: "They were too slow. They were walking, they were jogging, there was not enough urgency in the game."

Sports.title: Longest serving manager in Scotland leaves after misconduct investigation
Sports.content:
Longest serving manager in Scotland leaves after misconduct investigation

Scottish side The Spartans have parted ways with manager Dougie Samuel after 14 years following a misconduct investigation this month

View 2 Images Douglas Samuel has left The Spartans (Image: Instagram/The Spartans)

The longest-serving manager in Scottish football has left his club following allegations of misconduct. Dougie Samuel has left The Spartans FC after 14 years at the helm.

‌



Earlier this month, it was announced that the 59-year-old would be taking a period of 'extended leave' from the club. Now, the Edinburgh-based club have confirmed that Samuel has departed following an 'independent investigation into allegations of misconduct'.

‌



Paul Thomson was made interim head coach following Samuel's initial leave of absence and is set to continue in that role. Former Hibernian and Kilmarnock manager Mixu Paatelainen, the side's sporting director, has assisted the coaching staff this month.

‌



Samuel had led the club since 2012 and helped them progress from the Lowland League into the SPFL three years ago.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Following an independent investigation into allegations of misconduct, The Spartans FC Head Coach Douglas Samuel has left the club," a club statement read.

‌



"Out of respect for the privacy of the individuals involved, and in accordance with our confidentiality policies, we will make no further comment on the specific details of the investigation or its findings

"Paul Thomson will continue as our Interim Head Coach for the foreseeable future, we really appreciate the commitment of our coaching, medical and support teams plus our players through this busy spell with another game on Tuesday."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Spartans currently sit third in the fourth tier of Scottish football following the opening eight matches of the season. They lost 3-0 at Dumbarton in their most recent match.

Earlier this year, Samuel reflected on his time at The Spartans as he approached 5,000 days at the club.

"Absolutely not!" he said when asked if he expected to stay at the club for 14 years. "I'm not somebody who sort of looks that far ahead in my life.

‌



"I've got goals and aspirations, but I try to live my life in the moment, in the present. It's very difficult, you know. I think the reality is that it's a part-time job in name, but certainly not in nature.

View 2 Images Douglas Samuel was successful at The Spartans in his 14-year spell (Image: Instagram/The Spartans)

"If you want to be a success at any level, you're thinking about it, you're working on it almost every day.

‌



"But I had a massive warning in my early 50s. I suffered a heart attack. I was doing two jobs full-time and I was probably doing too much.

"I was in a spin class. I fainted on my bike. I had a heart attack and my wife was on the bike next to me, so that was obviously quite a traumatic experience. But it’s probably one of the best things that ever happened to me - I was very lucky that it then revealed that I needed some treatment. I got a couple of stents fitted.

"It was a real wake-up call. I was very, very lucky and from that day onwards, I've tried to have a better balance and crucially keep perspective because I think sometimes we forget that it is the beautiful game, but it is a game.

Article continues below

"It's no life or death and I think it's important that we have perspective and that we try and enjoy the journey and enjoy the experiences.

"Of course, it matters a great deal to a great deal of people. But it is still a game and I think it's important to remember that at times. But I'm driven because life's about purpose as well. We try and leave a legacy."

Sports.title: Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute after his mum's death
Sports.content:
Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute after his mum's death

Ronald Koeman Jr, the son of ex-Everton manager Ronald Koeman, cut an emotional figure after a tribute was made to his late mother while playing for Telstar

View 3 Images Ronald Koeman Jr in tears after his mum died earlier this week (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

Ronald Koeman Jr broke down in tears following an emotional tribute to his mother after she died earlier this week.

‌



Koeman Jr's father, Ronald Koeman, announced in an Instagram post on Tuesday that his wife, Bartina Koeman-Boddeveld, passed away at the age of 65 after a long battle with cancer.

‌



Koeman said: "With intense sadness, but also with great pride and love, we say goodbye to my beautiful wife, our dearest mom and grandma. Bartina Koeman-Boddeveld. January 30 - September 15 2026. Familie Koeman."

‌



The couple had been married for 41 years and have three children together. Koeman Jr is one of his three children, with Tim Koeman his eldest and Debbie Koeman the only daughter.

Premier League star's partner sends message to Thomas Tuchel after England snub READ MORE :

Koeman Jr, who is a professional goalkeeper for Dutch side Telstar, played his first game since his mum died on Sunday afternoon, as his team went up against AZ Alkmaar.

In tribute to Koeman-Boddeveld, AZ stopped the game in the 12th minute for a minutes applause and during that they put a photo up of the 65-year-old on the big screen.

‌



Unsurprisingly, that drew an emotional reaction from Koeman Jr, who had to wipe the tears away as the whole stadium stood up and clapped in tribute of his mum.

3 View 3 Images (Image: ESPN) 3 View 3 Images (Image: ESPN)

‌



Footage from ESPN also showed Telstar head coach Henk Brugge in tears following what has been a difficult week for the Koeman family, including his goalkeeper.

AZ ended up going on to win the match 1-0 with Mexx Meerdink striking the decisive blow in the first-half, leaving Koeman Jr's side down in 13th with just one league win all season.

Koeman Jr has spent the last five years at Telstar, after moving to the club from Oss in 2021. The 31-year-old has since made 165 appearances for the IJmuiden side, who won promotion to Eredivisie in 2024/25.

‌



His father, Koeman Sr, meanwhile, had his wife alongside him throughout his legendary football career. The defender was one of the best players of his generation and scored the winning goal in the 1992 European Cup final, which saw Barcelona beat Sampdoria.

After hanging up his boots, the Dutchman went into management and recently had been in charge of his national side, but stepped down this summer after their World Cup exit, making it clear that his wife's circumstances had given him a new perspective.

He said: "The past years have made me realise again that there are more important things than football. Football has been my life, but health is priceless.

Article continues below

"When someone you love is fighting a tough battle, your perspective changes. My wife Bartina has supported and encouraged me every day to finish my work as a national coach, despite her own illness process. That is a testimony to incredible strength. I appreciate her more than I’ll ever be able to put into words."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick explains Benjamin Sesko absence vs Fulham as Man Utd suffer fresh blow
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick explains Benjamin Sesko absence vs Fulham as Man Utd suffer fresh blow

Benjamin Sesko didn't travel with the Manchester United squad for their Premier League clash with Fulham and Michael Carrick has confirmed the reason for his absence

View 2 Images Manchester United were without Benjamin Sesko at Fulham (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United are assessing Benjamin Sesko after the striker picked up an injury, Michael Carrick has confirmed. Sesko, 23, missed Sunday's clash with Fulham, having not travelled to London with the rest of Carrick's squad.

‌



The Slovenia international was subbed off in the second half of Wednesday's woeful 3-2 loss at home to Brighton in the Carabao Cup. It's possible that the setback is a reoccurrence of the shin injury which he first sustained during a clash with Liverpool in May and ruled him out of pre-season.

‌



When asked for an update before kick-off at Craven Cottage, Carrick replied: "A little bit of an assessment at the moment. He pulled up after the game the other day with a little bit of pain, so we'll have to see how he is."

‌



Sesko featured in United's first six matches of the season, starting two. He scored in games against Everton and Sabah.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Sesko is now a doubt for his country's Nations League fixtures against Scotland, North Macedonia and Switzerland during the international break. The ex-RB Leipzig star was called up by Slovenia manager Bostjan Cesar earlier this week.

Carrick hoped to have Sesko at his disposal for what was billed as a must-win game, as Matheus Cunha started up front instead. After mustering just four points from their opening four Premier League games, the pressure was on the Red Devils boss.

"I know the club, I know the role, I know what's expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard, playing at a certain level, achieving certain things on the pitch," Carrick said.

‌



"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, that's just totally not in my thinking, not one part of it. Like, how long I've got. It's ridiculous to think that way in a position that I'm in, that's just not on the radar.

Should Manchester United have signed a striker? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick needs results to ease the pressure on him (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Article continues below

"I understand what we need to achieve and where we need to be as a football club for the owners, what they expect, for the supporters as much as anything… there's not [much] more important for me than what they expect and what they want to see. I get all that.

"It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results and two or three games too many because I really hate losing. But that doesn't mean that the world caves in. In some minds, it does. It can't for us because we've got to perform, we've got to get wins and we've got a lot of games to plan for. That's exactly what we're doing."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher talks up two Liverpool transfers who could follow Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher talks up two Liverpool transfers who could follow Andoni Iraola

Liverpool hired Andoni Iraola in the summer off the back of his impressive work at Bournemouth, with the new Reds boss tipped to possibly raid his former club

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has talked up some potential transfer targets for Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has suggested that Liverpool could go after Alex Scott or Rayan given their previous history with Andoni Iraola.

The Reds are in the midst of their new era under the Spaniard, who moved to Anfield off the back of three impressive years with the Cherries. Iraola's final season saw him lead Bournemouth into Europe for the first time, with Scott and Rayan among his top performers.

Bournemouth have sold their top players annually for huge profits - last season they offloaded Antoine Semenyo and prior to that had let Milos Kerkez head to Liverpool.

The Cherries dug their heels in over the summer and were determined to keep Scott despite links with Chelsea and Manchester United. Rayan, who was named in Brazil's World Cup squad, is another Carragher has hailed as he suggested Iraola may use his links to bring them to Merseyside.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

He said of Scott on Sky Sports: "I think he’s a wonderful player. There was a lot of interest in him in the summer and because Liverpool have a former Bournemouth manager, you almost think: will there be a link or will there be a couple of players moving that way?

"I thought Rayan was fantastic last season as well. It will have been really good for him to get a goal in midweek because he probably hasn’t been himself at the start of the season. There are some fantastic players here at Bournemouth."

Kerkez was among the players to shine at the Vitality Stadium under Iraola, which prompted Liverpool to go after him. However the full-back has struggled at Anfield with his new boss looking to unlock the form he showed so regularly two seasons ago.

View 2 Images Alex Scott and Rayan are two of Bournemouth's leading lights

Scott could prove to be a target come the summer with Liverpool's midfield copping criticism this term. Iraola has the likes of Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister to choose from, whilst Florian Wirtz has been deployed centrally as the team's No 10.

A move for Rayan is less likely given the recent investment in the team's frontline. Bradley Barcola recently became Liverpool's third £100m plus signing over the last two summers, joining Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz are also forward options for Iraola.

Liverpool were victorious at the Vitality on Sunday afternoon, beating Bournemouth 1-0 thanks to a strike from Alexander Isak.

Sports.title: Middlesex beat Leicestershire Foxes to end 36-year List A trophy wait
Sports.content:
Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge.

Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.

Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

Leicestershire, still reeling from the points deduction in the Rothesay County Championship that makes relegation almost certain, had hoped to ease the pain winning a second Metro Bank trophy in the space of four seasons but it was not to be.

Put in, Middlesex were 32-3 in the 11th over and five down in the 22nd - all snared by the immaculate Cox.

Image: Middlesex's players celebrate winning the Metro Bank One Day Cup

Nathan Fernandes slashed at one from Holland, who dismissed Max Holden in similar fashion, and Tom Scriven found a thin edge to remove skipper Ben Geddes for a duck.

Josh De Caires fell victim to a superb leg-side grab before Luke Hollman nicked a first-ball googly from Rehan Ahmed and Cox celebrated again.

But Duke - on loan from Yorkshire as cover for the injured Joe Cracknell - provided the support Higgins needed before a top edge to extra cover brought his undoing, Helm was leg before to Rehan and Higgins perished one ball after going to his maiden List A hundred, failing to clear long-on, looking for a 10th boundary.

Image: Middlesex wicketkeeper Harry Duke played a crucial innings

The Leicestershire innings almost exactly mirrored that of Middlesex as they slipped to 32-3 and 79-5.



Sharma dismissed Foxes captain and former Middlesex batter Stephen Eskinazi, caught at second slip, and Hamza Shaikh leg before, veteran Roland-Jones having Rishi Patel caught at deep square leg.

Roland-Jones claimed two more victims in Ahmed, leg before, and Cox, caught behind.

Leicestershire found themselves needing someone to step up as Higgins had and Kelly answered the call. Allowing few scoring opportunities to pass him by, reaching 50 from 52 balls with six fours and a pick-up for six off Sharma as he and Holland added 50 for the sixth wicket.

Ben Green's departure added more pressure, with 57 still needed. Kelly, who twice hammered Zafar down the ground for more sixes, kept the Foxes in the hunt, reaching 100 from 103 balls.

But, after needing treatment for cramp, he pulled Helm straight to deep square. Ajaz Patel fell to a stunning catch at backward point by Zafar off Helm, before Scriven was the last man to go, caught at mid-off.

Sports.title: Smith thrashes Price to win World Series after Littler's shock exit
Sports.content:
Ross Smith thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become World Series of Darts champion, while Luke Littler's hopes of a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was dashed in the quarter-finals.

Smith won the last six legs, fired in 11 maximums, recorded back-to-back ton-plus finishes and went at 46 per cent on his doubles as he overwhelmed Price in Amsterdam on Sunday night to add this silverware to his 2022 European Championship in Dortmund.

Price, who missed a host of doubles in the back end of the match as his checkout percentage dropped to 26, has seven PDC majors in total, including three Grand Slams and the 2021 World Championship, but none since the World Series Finals in 2022.

Speaking bluntly afterwards on ITV4, the Welshman said: "I am playing some good darts, I am earning some good money. If I never win a major again I really don't care as long as I am doing well.

"I am gutted I've lost but if I never win another major then I have a good family, I have invested all my money. I really don't mind. I will be gutted for half an hour but on Tuesday I'll be in Tenerife.

"I was absolute rubbish in that final but don't take anything away from Ross. He was brilliant and took his opportunities."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 is over after defeat to Jonny Clayton at the World Series of Darts Finals

Smith stars in Amsterdam as Littler crashes out

While Smith celebrates his fifth trophy of the season - this triumph in the Netherlands follows the Hungarian Darts Open and International Darts Open on the European Tour and a couple of Players Championship events - Littler is processing a shock defeat.

Having won the first five majors of the year - as well as the World Cup of Darts alongside Luke Humphries - Littler was hoping to claim all 11 this year, only to be trounced 10-4 by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals.

Smith overcame Josh Rock in the last eight before dumping out remaining home hope Gian van Veen in the last four, while Price surged towards the end of matches to eliminate James Wade and Clayton before being floored by Smith.

Image: Smith can now celebrate his second PDC major title

Smith said: "It feels a bit mad, to be fair! I am absolutely made up with the win. I am so happy. [Price] is one of the best in the world, so to beat him you have to up your game.

"I always say in my interviews that I take each game as it comes. I play one game at a time. They are all finals and I give it my all. That is working for me at the moment."

Sports.title: Hits and misses: Maresca's Man City serve up pure chaos as Gakpo shines
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester City and Sunderland

Man City's captivating but chaotic 5-3 win over Sunderland could not have been further removed from the picture of control so often associated with City under Pep Guardiola. "We want to control but the other team don't want to allow us," Enzo Maresca reflected.

Sunderland made command of the game very difficult, but City equally did themselves no favours.

Maresca had warned of the size of the task pre-match - and so it proved. "I knew how good they are, off the ball very aggressive," he added, after the Black Cats terrorised the Etihad. Rarely have City conceded so much territory or given up so many chances at home, nor do they often ship three goals.

Why were they so open?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brian Brobbey scores for Sunderland at Man City

Brian Brobbey served up another masterclass in hold-up play, just as he did against Arsenal last week. Except on this occasion he matched his physical presence with three excellent goals. Every time Brobbey won his duel against Ruben Dias - which was often - there was space to play off.

He was joined in waves of attack by Enzo Le Fee, before Nilson Angulo and Thomas Meunier swiftly arrived from wide. Suddenly City were overloaded. And it happened time after time. Neither Elliot Anderson nor Enzo Fernandez could get to grips with the physical battle, unable to cope when Sunderland pressed man to man or played longer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brobbey completes his hat-trick in a losing cause for Sunderland

City were out-duelled by a substantial amount, outrun too. Brobbey won 10 of the 12 duels he contested and drew a game-high five fouls. He could not be shackled, a clear winner of the tug-of-war.

But fortunately for Maresca, City were able to play Sunderland at their own game for enough of the match to score five times themselves. They picked on mistakes, digging deep to get the job done the anti-Pep way. Imperfect but effective.

Perhaps that should count for something, too.

Laura Hunter

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Fulham and Manchester United.

Michael Carrick is getting a reputation for the way he calmly bats away criticism of his Man Utd team, contrasting with the noise of those detractors. He has had to do that more and more in the past week, with a Manchester derby loss followed by a Carabao Cup collapse, and now a scrambled point at previously bottom-club Fulham.



At Craven Cottage he was asked about United's joint-worst start to a Premier League season and pointed to fine margins. The 25-yard stunner at Everton, the incorrectly awarded City goal, the bizarre own goal at Fulham and two strikes against posts earlier in the game. He has a point.

But the problem is the accumulation of poor performances is starting to add up. As Carrick would say, it's not been all bad in any game but the positives are being outweighed by United's shortcomings. Physically, defensively, and in possession United have been found wanting in key moments and keep paying the price.

A 10-point gap has already yawned open to table-topping City and the prospect of United improving on last season's third place seems unrealistic right now.



"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick defiantly told the press on Sunday evening. But a big shift, encompassing more than just finer details in a game, is required if it's to be a successful one.

Peter Smith

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Bournemouth and Liverpool

In every single Liverpool game he has started this season, Cody Gakpo has produced a golden moment in front of goal.

A goal at Newcastle on the opening weekend, a silky assist against Nottingham Forest, assists for both goals in the win over Ipswich, another one and a goal against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup - but this intervention in the 1-0 win at Bournemouth was the best of the lot.

With Liverpool struggling for attacking influence, Gakpo's hard-fought run and cross down the right wing was vital in the build-up to Alexader Isak's winner. "The difficult part of the goal is from him," said Iraola about Gakpo, who is unfortunate not to be accredited with the assist.

Image: Alexander Isak celebrates with Cody Gakpo

But Gakpo also starred defensively at Bournemouth, winning more duels than any other player on the pitch. He shut down one of the Cherries' biggest threats. "I know Adrien Truffert very well and he demands a lot from you defensively. Cody has been very important in both ways," added Iraola.

When Gakpo is absent, Liverpool are not the same team - as seen in the goalless draw with Fulham where the Dutchman was only fit enough for the bench.

Looking at this form, it is absolutely staggering that Liverpool considered sanctioning the sale of Gakpo this summer. Where would they be without him?

Sam Blitz

From the highs of their first win in Europe against Real Sociedad on Thursday to the lows of yet another defeat in the Premier League.

Bournemouth now go into the three-week international break without a win. A sour note to leave on given the joy that followed from their victory in San Sebastian.

Neither side impressed at the Vitality Stadium and for the most part, the Cherries looked the more likely team to go on and snatch three points.

But with Justin Kluivert sidelined through injury and no other changes made from the team in midweek, they just did not have the legs to go one step further in front of goal.

Marco Rose has made just two changes to their Premier League starting XIs this season, the fewest of any side.

That is not sustainable while balancing European football. Rotation is needed to keep this squad fit; otherwise they risk slipping into an unwanted relegation battle this season.

Patrick Rowe

Alvaro Arbeloa says Fulham are improving and it is a fair assessment after draws against Liverpool and Man Utd at the end of a testing start in the Premier League.

A third consecutive defeat in early September at home to Crystal Palace heightened concerns Fulham may be in a relegation fight after four trouble-free seasons under Marco Silva, but they have something to build on heading into the international break.

Josh King has been their brightest player across the first five games with two goals and is showing why he is so highly regarded by the club having come through the academy. David Affengruber, an £8.5m summer signing from Elche, shone on debut at centre-back against Liverpool and appears to have dislodged Joachim Andersen for now.

Gonzalo Garcia scored on the opening day of the season following his move from Real Madrid but has managed just two shots on target from 15 so far.

The next six weeks will be pivotal for Arbeloa. He has more time to work with his squad now ahead of fixtures against the three newly-promoted clubs when the season resumes.

David Richardson

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Leeds United and Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace arrived at Elland Road with 11 goals conceded from their opening four Premier League games. They left with a clean sheet and, on balance in the second half, will probably feel they could have taken all three points.

This was a spirited, disciplined performance from Palace. They came out after the break with a completely different mindset and put Leeds under pressure.

Leeds were strangely flat. Dominic Calvert-Lewin was starved of service for long periods and even when the chances did arrive, Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez was there to deny him.

In the end, 0-0 felt like a reflection of two sides who cancelled each other out, but Palace can take far more encouragement from this performance than Leeds can.

For Pierre Sage, though, this is the sort of defensive display he will hope can become the foundation of a turnaround.

William Bitibiri

Sports.title: 'I deserve to be in!' - Spaun uses Team USA snub as fuel for Wentworth win
Sports.content:
JJ Spaun said he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" during his BMW PGA Championship win and used being snubbed by Team USA's Presidents Cup side as motivation for his Wentworth victory.

Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira.

Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spaun reflected on his debut win at the BMW PGA Championship and how the 'stars aligned' for him

Spaun was controversially overlooked for a captain's pick by Brandt Snedeker in his line-up to face the International Team in the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports, with the 36-year-old pleased to respond by claiming a statement victory.

"The stars aligned this week for me to come out on top," Spaun said. "I'm just grateful to have the opportunity and play well and give myself a chance and came out with a W.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manuel Elvira handed Spaun victory after a nightmare double-bogey on the final hole at Wentworth

"We [him and Snedeker] haven't spoken. I played with a huge chip on my shoulder. I definitely had something to prove this week, but everything happens for a reason. I'm so delighted to be here and just to even play this event.

"The extra motivation, I think that is the willpower that you have. Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple weeks ago was very disappointing and I wanted to prove that I deserve to be on that team.

"I took care of my business this week, so all the best to the team next week at Medinah - I'll be watching from my couch!"

Sports.title: Neville: Carrick has got to stop defending the players
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has urged Michael Carrick to stop defending Manchester United players after another troubling performance in their draw at Fulham.

While on Sky Sports co-commentary, Neville described their start to the second half at Craven Cottage as "the worst 15 minutes I have ever seen Manchester United play".

In that time, Carrick's side conceded a horror own goal from Lisandro Martinez, before Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike avoided a third straight league defeat.

The 1-1 draw followed losses to Manchester City last Sunday and a capitulation in the Carabao Cup third round against Brighton while there was a lack of urgency and energy at times from Man Utd in west London although Carrick dismissed the idea that his side were "passive".
