World.title: Government Rejects EU Parliament Resolution on Zambia’s Post-Election Situation
World.content:
Government has rejected as premature and insufficiently informed, the European Parliament Resolution on Zambia’s post-election situation, adopted on September 17, 2026 under an urgency procedure.

In a statement issued by Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Minister Mulambo Haimbe in New York, Government says the resolution was adopted without prior engagement with the Zambian Government and before the publication of the European Union Election Observation Mission’s final report.

Government says serious determinations concerning a sovereign state should be based on verified facts and engagement with the concerned government.

It has consequently requested the EU Delegation in Lusaka to convene a formal partnership dialogue with the European Commission and the European External Action Service.

On the death of former Cabinet Minister Mutotwe Kafwaya on August 14, Government says investigations by the Zambia Police Service are ongoing, with independent oversight by the Human Rights Commission.

Government says the bereaved family has also been offered participation in the postmortem through a legal representative and an independent pathologist.

On treason charges and access to justice, Government maintains that the Judiciary is independent and that all accused persons are entitled to due process, fair and impartial trials, legal representation, family visits and medical care.

It says decisions on bail and other court proceedings rest with the courts.

Government has also rejected allegations of arbitrary detention, saying official records do not support the figures cited by the European Parliament.

It maintains that arrests and detentions were conducted within Zambia’s constitutional and legal safeguards.

On the use of force by law enforcement, Government says force is permitted in certain circumstances, subject to necessity, proportionality and legal safeguards.

It argues that it would be premature to characterise specific incidents as murder before investigations are concluded.

Government further says the resolution does not sufficiently take into account ongoing investigations and judicial proceedings.

It has called on the European Parliament, European Commission, European External Action Service and cooperating partners to allow Zambia’s institutions to work independently and without undue influence.

Despite the disagreement, Government says Zambia remains committed to its strategic partnership with the European Union in areas including trade, investment, development and critical raw materials.

Government says it will continue engaging EU institutions to provide factual clarification and ensure Zambia’s position is accurately reflected.

World.title: Zambia, Ethiopia strengthen ties
World.content:
Permanent Secretary for Special Duties, Kennedy Kalunga has reaffirmed Zambia’s readiness to strengthen commercial and diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, mining, tourism, transport, and education.

Speaking during the official opening of the Honourary Consulate of Ethiopia in Lusaka and the 2019 New Year celebrations for that Country, Mr Kalunga noted that the platform would facilitate investment partnerships, trade missions and stronger economic linkages.

He urged business communities from both Zambia and Ethiopia to seize the opportunities presented by the consulate, expressing confidence that its establishment would foster greater cooperation.

“The consulate will connect our people through cultural exchange, education partnerships, tourism promotion and people-to-people interaction,”Mr Kalunga stated.

Speaking at the same event, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Ethiopia to Zambia and Zimbabwe, who is also Permanent Representative to COMESA, Mohammed Rashid also reaffirmed Ethiopia’s commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation with Zambia.

Mr Rashid cited growing partnerships in aviation, trade, investment, tourism and cultural exchange between the two Countries, such as the Ethiopian Airlines -Zambia Airways partnership as a practical example of expanding cooperation between the two countries.

“This is not only the opening of an office but the beginning of a new chapter of closer engagement with our community in Zambia,” he said.

Mr Rashid further highlighted the community’s role in shaping Ethiopia’s image abroad through business, professional and social engagement in strengthening relations with Zambia.

Earlier, Honourary Consul of Ethiopia to Zambia, Getenesh Aweke highlighted the new office will build a bridge for trade, investment, tourism, and cultural exchange between the two Countries.

She explained that apart from providing a symbolic home that honours Zambia while representing Ethiopia, She added that the Consulate will also provide assistance to Ethiopians living in this country.

“This office has been established to serve, to connect, and to strengthen the friendship between our two countries,” she said.

World.title: FRA reaches three million metric tonnes of Maize
World.content:
The Food Reserve Agency (FRA) has reached three million metric tonnes of maize in national strategic reserves, the highest level ever recorded in the country, with the milestone reached in September as the 2026 crop marketing season continues.

FRA Executive Director, Justin Chuunka says the rate at which maize is being purchased means the grain coming in is being secured, with the agency continuing to monitor purchases and storage capacity across the country.

Ministry of Information and Media Director Spokesperson, Henry Kapata, said the record stock comes as Government Implements President Hakainde Hichilema’s directive to secure enough maize locally and avoid relying on imports, following the food-security concerns created by the drought.

Mr Kapata has told the media in Lusaka that the Government has also been supporting the purchase of maize from farmers, with FRA having paid more than K6 billion to farmers by 28 August after purchasing over one million metric tonnes within days of the opening of the marketing season.

He says the three-million-tonnes reserve puts Zambia in a stronger position to meet domestic food requirements and maintain its position as a regional food basket.

World.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Meets Macron for Private Dinner in Paris
World.content:
According to Mr Onanuga, the dinner reflected the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and France.

President Bola Tinubu met French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday for a private dinner at the Élysée Palace in Paris.

It is the latest in the series of meetings and engagements between Nigeria and France since Mr Tinubu assumed office in 2023.

The president's Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed the meeting in a post on X on Friday. He also shared photographs of the two leaders at the French presidential palace.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the meeting took place while Mr Tinubu was in France during the second leg of his three-week annual leave in Europe.

He arrived in Paris on Monday after spending the first part of his leave in London.

According to Mr Onanuga, the dinner reflected the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and France.

In the post, he wrote, "French President Emmanuel Macron received President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a private dinner Thursday night at the Élysée Palace, reflecting the enduring relationship between Nigeria and France and their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation."

President Tinubu, in a separate post about the meeting, also said his conversation with Mr Macron reflects both countries' mutual interest in maintaining good relations and strengthening the existing partnership.

He also thanked the French president for his hospitality and friendship.

"It was a pleasure to share a private dinner with President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace in Paris. @EmmanuelMacron

"Our conversation reaffirmed the strong friendship between Nigeria and France, as well as our shared commitment to deepening cooperation and building a mutually beneficial partnership between our two nations," he wrote.

Photographs released from the dinner showed Mr Tinubu and Mr Macron together at the Élysée Palace, with another image showing Mr Tinubu, Mr Macron and France's First Lady, Brigitte Macron.

However, details of the interaction or any potential agreement between the two leaders were not provided.

World.title: Guinea: Guinea Bans France 24, Withdraws Jeune Afrique Correspondent's Accreditation
World.content:
Dakar — The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on Guinean authorities to reverse Thursday's ban on France 24 after a presenter called President Mamadi Doumbouya a "putschist president" and to reinstate the accreditation of the pan-African weekly Jeune Afrique's Guinea correspondent Diawo Barry.

"By prohibiting France 24 from broadcasting and Jeune Afrique's Diawo Barry from working, Guinean authorities have shown their ruthless determination to silence independent voices and to intimidate other media outlets into self-censorship," said Moussa Ngom, CPJ's Francophone Africa representative. "Authorities must immediately reverse these decisions and refrain from further actions that erode press freedom and the public's right to information."

In its September 17 decision, the regulatory High Authority of Communication (HAC) said it had banned France 24 because it had failed to comply with its order the previous day "to immediately cease using terms deemed derogatory to the dignity of the Head of State and to make the required editorial corrections." The HAC also withdrew press accreditation for all the French state-owned channel's correspondents, special correspondents, and contributors in Guinea.

On Monday, a France 24 presenter used the word "putschist" while commenting on Doumbouya's visit to Ivory Coast.



Hours after the HAC's September 16 notice, France 24 added an online correction to the video's description, saying that Doumbouya had been "mistakenly labeled a coup leader."

"Having seized power in a coup on September 5, 2021, which overthrew President Alpha Condé, he was subsequently elected President of the Republic following the presidential election of December 28, 2025," the correction said.

France 24 told Agence France-Presse news agency that it had also apologized and corrected the error on air.

Also on September 16, the HAC revoked Barry's accreditation as Jeune Afrique's correspondent on the grounds that his coverage of news in Guinea did not meet the requirements of objective, neutral, balanced reporting.

The Guinean satirical newspaper Le Lynx, where Barry is publishing director, suggested that Jeune Afrique's September special report on Guinea, "Democracy under surveillance," had "ruffled feathers."

Jeune Afrique said that the HAC's decision had been handed down "without prior consultation" and was "not based on any specific allegation" to support its "vague" accusations.

Since Doumbouya took power, the HAC has introduced long-term and indefinite bans on numerous critical outlets and reporters. The whereabouts of journalist Habib Marouane Camara, who was seized by uniformed men in 2024, and of exiled journalist Mamoudou Babila Keita's elderly father, Elhadj Adama Keita, who was kidnapped in 2025, remain unknown.

Close 

CPJ's calls to request comment from the HAC went unanswered.

World.title: Nigeria: Niger State Imposes 24-Hour Curfew After Suspects Die in Custody
World.content:
The Niger State Government has imposed a 24-hour curfew across Minna, the state capital, as tension rises over the deaths of about 37 suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).

The curfew takes effect immediately after Juma'at prayers on Friday, the government announced.

The government has also ordered the suspension of all mining activities in the state until further notice.

The directives are part of the state government's measures to address the prevailing security situation and restore safety across the state.



The government advised residents to remain indoors and comply fully with the curfew and other security directives until further notice.

The government also cancelled an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally scheduled for Minna on Saturday and suspended the NSCDC State Commandant, Suberu Aniviye, and his team.

Governor Mohammed Bago announced the measures during a press briefing in Minna on Friday.

He said the curfew was necessary to prevent a breakdown of law and order and to allow the government to manage the situation while investigations continue.

Background to the curfew

The deaths occurred after the NSCDC detained suspects arrested in connection with mining activities in the Ema Ushishi area of Niger State.

More than 37 detainees reportedly died while in custody, although the exact number and cause of the deaths have not been officially established.

The bodies were later moved to a mortuary, a development that heightened tension among youths and residents in Minna.

The incident triggered public concern and fears of possible protests or violence, prompting the state government to cancel the APC rally and impose the curfew.

Mr Bago described the deaths as tragic and unacceptable and said the government had begun steps to establish what happened.

He announced the constitution of a committee of inquiry to investigate the incident and determine the cause of the deaths.

Cause of death not established

The governor cautioned against concluding the forensic examinations, medical assessments, and autopsies.

He said possible causes being considered included suffocation caused by overcrowding in the detention facility and exposure to hazardous substances allegedly linked to illegal mining.

"There is no official root cause of these deaths yet. It is too early for anybody to conclude the root causes," Mr Bago said.

He said the state government was compiling a register of the deceased to identify and contact their families.

Mr Bago assured the victims' relatives that the government would engage with them and provide the necessary support during the investigation.

NSCDC commandant suspended

The governor announced the immediate suspension of Mr Aniviye and his team to allow for an impartial investigation.

He said the suspension was not a declaration of guilt but a measure to ensure that the investigation was conducted without interference.

The governor said the Director-General of the NSCDC, who is currently outside the country, had delegated his deputy to represent him in engagements concerning the incident.

He added that the state government had already met with the senior NSCDC official.

'We will probe deeply'

Mr Bago pledged that the government would investigate the incident thoroughly and ensure that those responsible for any wrongdoing were held accountable.

"Lives of human beings are lives of human beings. Such an unjust government will not tolerate any injustice, and we are going to make sure that we probe this thing deeply until we get to the root of this," he said.

He urged residents, particularly youths, to remain calm and obey the curfew.

Close 

"We are calling on all the youth to please stay away from violence. It is not going to bring about those who have died. It will rather cost us a lot at the end of the day," he said.

Mining suspended

The governor also ordered the closure of activities at the illegal mining site in Ema Ushishi.

He expressed concern over mining operations conducted without adequate technology, safety equipment and protective gear.

According to him, such practices expose miners to dangerous conditions and may have contributed to the incident.

The state government said it would continue to work with the NSCDC, the police, the State Security Service and other relevant agencies to establish the facts.

Mr Bago commiserated with the families of the deceased and declared three days of mourning in the state.

He said the cancellation of the APC rally was intended to allow the state to mourn the victims and focus on restoring calm and completing the investigation.

World.title: Algeria: Algeria Shifts Towards English As French Loses Ground in Schools
World.content:
Primary school pupils in Algeria are in for a change this year when, for the first time, the national curriculum will focus on English over French. The move follows a general trend across former French colonies in North Africa that are now prioritising English.

Algeria's 2026-27 school year kicks off next week with a change: a shift away from its usual focus on French as a second language.

Introduced in primary schools alongside French in 2022, from now on English will be the first foreign language children study.

Algerian education minister Mohamed Seghir Saadaoui announced in July that English classes would begin in the third year of primary school, when children are around 8. French lessons will follow a year later.



"In third year, only English will be taught," Saadaoui said.

Colonial baggage

The reform is part of a broader shift towards English in Algeria, where French remains closely tied to the country's colonial history.

In a paper published earlier this year, Algerian linguist Fadhila Leroul of the Mouloud Mammeri University of Tizi-Ouzou says the change can be explained not only by English's status as a global lingua franca, but because in the political context of former French colonies cutting ties from France, it steers Algeria "beyond the colonial legacy attached to French".

Algeria's history with France is long and tightly knit. Algeria was under French rule from 1830 to 1962, and was formally incorporated into France in 1848.

The French language was imposed everywhere from administration to formal education, but French was not accessible to just anyone. Arabic remained the language of the majority, while French was for Europeans and those with access to education.

According to Abu Bakr Khaled Saad Allah, an Algerian professor and researcher on higher education, this division made language deeply bound up with questions of national identity. Algerian writer Kateb Yacine, who wrote in French, once described the language as a "war trophy" taken from the former colonial power.

How a Nigerian town came to speak 'street French'

Following its independence, Algeria pursued policies to make Arabic the official national language. Arabic has been the country's primary language ever since, but for decades French remained prevalent in academia.

Algiers began toying with the idea of pushing English in the early 1990s, when primary school students were given the choice between English and French as a second language.

The plan was shut down and English was taken off the syllabus until 2019, when the minister of education put forward a plan to promote the use of English in universities. In 2022, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune announced that English would be introduced in primary schools.

The move coincided with a weakening of Algeria's relations with France. The relationship between the two countries has been tense since 2021 and, despite a period of rapprochement in 2023, worsened in 2024 after France declared its support for Morocco's sovereignty over the disputed Western Sahara.

The last word: why half of the world's languages could vanish this century

Regional shift

Both Morocco and Tunisia also took pains post-independence to cut ties to their former colonial power.

Morocco was a French protectorate from 1912 to 1956. Under Paris, French was the only language used for instruction. When Morocco got its independence, it steered the country towards policies of Arabisation to ensure Arabic once again took a central place.

The Moroccan government progressively introduced Arabic into primary education, but French remained the language of higher study, particularly in mathematics and science.

In the 2000s, the kingdom began to move towards a more multilingual model that supported both Arabic and French. At the same time, English was cementing its dominance as a global language - particular with younger generations.

One 2021 survey of 15-25-year-olds, commissioned by the British Council, found 40 percent of respondents believed English was the most important language to learn, compared to only 10 percent for French. As one participant said: "Everyone is turning to the English language because of its dominance on the internet."

By 2023, the Moroccan government began introducing English in public schools, where before it had been limited mainly to private institutions.

Close 

French overtakes Arabic to become world's fourth most spoken language

Tunisia was also a French protectorate from 1881 to 1956. The colonial rulers soon established a public education system that prioritised French, and it became the language of administration and economy. Those seeking access to higher opportunities therefore became bilingual in both French and Arabic.

After its independence, unlike Morocco and Algeria, Tunisia did not seek to cut out French from education and daily life. While it also pursued a policy of Arabisation, it maintained strong links with French education. The language of its former colonisers remained important in science, medicine, higher education, business and government.

But in contrast to its neighbours, Tunisia introduced English early on after independence as a foreign-language option in schools. Decades on, young people are increasingly choosing it.

In a 2020 Afrobarometer survey, around 68 percent of Tunisian respondents said English was the most important language for young people to learn. Only some 13 percent chose French.

World.title: Africa: Can Africa Turn Red Sea Rivalries to Its Advantage?
World.content:
A map of ports in the Horn of Africa.

analysis

Growing competition for African ports and security partnerships offers new leverage - if countries can avoid deeper geopolitical fragmentation.

Ongoing conflict in the Middle East exposes shifting regional geopolitical fault lines that are pulling African states into an emerging macro-conflict system anchored along the Red Sea.

This stems from several overlapping crises arising from US and Israeli military offensives against Iran and renewed Houthi attacks on shipping lanes, Saudi-Emirati competition across the Horn of Africa, and disputes amongst African states over sovereignty and regional influence.

Should these crises deepen and become self-reinforcing, the implications for African states across much of the Red Sea littoral could be dire.



The most recent US and Israeli offensive against Iran has added to these dynamics. Iran's retaliatory offensives against Gulf actors have called into question longstanding presumptions about the US' reliability in providing security for its traditional Gulf allies.

That in turn has precipitated more overt hedging strategies among regional powers, most notably the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia. Their prior security coordination to counter Iranian influence has buckled under the weight of opposing conceptions of regional order and claims to regional leadership.

Abu Dhabi projects power through expansive investments in ports and infrastructure, and through ties to non-state armed actors and secessionist movements in Yemen, Sudan, Libya and Somalia. It has also deepened engagement with Israel since normalising relations with Jerusalem under the 2020 Abraham Accords.

Riyadh has sought to undercut Abu Dhabi's efforts by backing recognised central state authorities and building countervailing partnerships with like-minded regional actors. Its closer coordination with Egypt, Pakistan and Turkey points to its growing efforts to reinforce state-centric alliances, constrain the UAE and hedge against Abu Dhabi's close ties with Israel.

This fluid security environment raises the stakes for African states along the Red Sea, which can offer access to ports, airfields, intelligence and security partnerships.

Landlocked Ethiopia seeks sea access to reduce its heavy dependence on Djibouti. Somaliland's Berbera port appealed because the Emirati-owned logistics company DP World had already developed the port, an economic zone and a transport corridor to Ethiopia.

But since the controversial 2024 Ethiopia-Somaliland cooperation memorandum, Ethiopia and Somalia recommitted to each other's territorial integrity in the Turkish-brokered Ankara Declaration, agreeing to negotiate Ethiopian commercial sea access under Somalia's sovereign authority.

This has not, however, removed Ethiopia from Gulf competition. Turkey has become an important mediator between Ethiopia and Somalia, while the UAE retains deep commercial and political ties with Ethiopia and Somaliland.

Meanwhile, 2026 reports of UAE-linked training and logistics networks supporting Sudan's Rapid Support Forces (RSF) from Ethiopian territory (which both Ethiopia and the UAE deny) have heightened regional tensions.

Africa's Red Sea States

Egypt, by contrast, controls the Suez Canal, has substantial military and naval capabilities and is strategically positioned at the Red Sea's northern end. Disruption around the Bab al-Mandab Strait directly hits Suez traffic and Egyptian revenues, while instability in Sudan and Somalia weighs heavily on Cairo's security interests.

Egypt's long-standing rivalry with Ethiopia has drawn Cairo into closer alignment with Saudi Arabia. Tensions have escalated since the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam was inaugurated in September 2025 and Ethiopia revived plans for three more dams on the Blue Nile.

Cairo has responded by working to undercut Addis Ababa, opposing Ethiopia's sea-access claims and unilateral control over Blue Nile waters, and bolstering ties with Eritrea.

Sudan's value to Gulf actors lies in both its war and its geography. Port Sudan is a crucial gateway for the weapons, logistics and personnel inflows sustaining the conflict. The UAE faces persistent allegations of backing the RSF, which it denies, while Egypt and Saudi Arabia have generally kept closer ties with the Sudanese Armed Forces.

Somalia's federal government decision in January 2026 to cut ties with the UAE was rejected by breakaway Somaliland and autonomous Puntland (and Jubaland), all of which have their own Emirati relationships. Turkey, Qatar and Saudi Arabia, however, have deepened engagement with the federal government.

Europe also has a role in this complex security landscape. The European Union (EU) maintains a substantial maritime presence through Operation ASPIDES, which protects commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, and Operation ATALANTA, which covers the Western Indian Ocean and parts of the Red Sea.

A July 2026 EU-Djibouti agreement on ASPIDES underlines European navies' reliance on African partners for access, logistics and onshore support.

In Somalia, the EU runs a civilian capacity-building mission and a military training mission, alongside anti-piracy initiatives. It is building maritime law enforcement and coast-guard capacity in Mogadishu, Somaliland and Puntland, with an emphasis on accountable security institutions and maritime governance.

This is a very different model of influence from the Gulf powers, who attach their support to greater access to ports, political patronage and strategic infrastructure in the Horn.

As African states along the Red Sea are pulled into the geopolitical orbit of rival Gulf powers, how sustainable are these partnerships and how might they change?

Gulf investment in ports, logistics, energy and other strategic infrastructure will probably continue, spurring deeper defence and security coordination. Commercial deals may become increasingly bundled with defence, security and intelligence commitments - a more compelling offer than anything Europe can provide.

The risk, however, is that African states become entrenched in rival security architectures and geopolitical alignments that narrow their room for manoeuvre.

Close 

This leaves Africa's Red Sea countries facing a policy dilemma. They could engage Middle Eastern powers through a coordinated approach that channels external competition towards a common development agenda. Or they could continue the current fragmented bilateral engagements that provide immediate investment, diplomatic backing and help with pressing security-related concerns.

But the short-term gains of bilateralism come at the expense of longer-term shared development and stability.

The African Union could help by assigning North and East African states a leading role in shaping the continent's engagement with Middle Eastern powers. Their proximity to the Red Sea and growing value to external players give them outsized access and influence that could be exercised on the continent's behalf.

The central question is whether Africa will harness this new value to advance shared development or allow it to deepen the continent's fragmentation.

This article was first published in Africa Tomorrow, the blog of the ISS' African Futures and Innovation programme.

Priyal Singh, ISS Senior Research Consultant and Signal Risk Geopolitical Analyst

World.title: East Africa: East Africa's Iconic Snow Peaks Face Imminent Extinction
World.content:
EAST Africa's iconic equatorial glaciers across three mountain peaks in Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania will soon disappear entirely, with new climate assessments predicting total extinction within three to five years.

According to the 2025 State of the Climate in Africa report, ice coverage on Mount Kenya Africa's second-highest peak has plummeted by 96 per cent over the past 115 years. The rapid retreat highlights a broader, unprecedented ecological shift affecting Mount Kilimanjaro in northern Tanzania and the Rwenzori Mountains situated on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Rainer Prinz, a climate scientist specializing in glacierclimate relationships, warns that the current rate of ice loss falls completely outside natural historical variations. "

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

During the past decade, we recorded a 40 to 60 per cent loss in East Africa's total glacier area meaning nearly half of the continent's equatorial ice melted in just ten years," Prinz explains, adding that while these glaciers may be as old as 10,000 years, the physical ice itself is considerably younger and rapidly disappearing.

Contrary to popular belief, these high-altitude glaciers do not act as regional water towers or major reservoirs for surrounding populations.

Prinz points out that the ice bodies are geographically too small to have a significant effect on downstream river systems.

Furthermore, a large portion of the ice loss occurs not through direct melting, but through sublimation a process where extreme dry air at high mountain altitudes converts solid ice directly into atmospheric vapor without producing liquid runoff.

On Mount Kenya, total glacier area measured approximately 69,000 square meters in 2022, holding roughly 500,000 cubic meters of ice.

If that entire volume were melted at once and distributed evenly across the mountain, the resulting water would equal no more than a single heavy rainfall event.

The true water towers of East Africa, scientists emphasize, are its montane forests rather than its summit ice caps.

Instead, the primary value of these tropical glaciers lies in their scientific importance as atmospheric indicators.

Functioning as natural instruments, glaciers translate complex, short-term weather patterns into long-term climate signals.

Located 5,000 to 6,000 meters above sea level in the mid-tropical troposphere, they provide vital data about atmospheric conditions in a highaltitude zone where traditional weather measurements are extremely scarce.

Research into these climate signals shows that the centurylong recession of East African glaciers is driven primarily by a steady decline in annual snowfall rather than direct temperature increases.

This drop in precipitation is triggered by shifting sea surface temperature patterns in the Indian Ocean caused by global warming. Warmer and colder ocean surface pockets alter atmospheric currents, reducing the transport of moist air masses toward East Africa.

Consequently, the lack of fresh white snow cover leaves bare, darker ice exposed to sunlight, lowering solar reflectivity and absorbing more solar energy, which further accelerates the retreat.

ASO READ: Six to represent Tanzania at Miss Tourism East Africa finals

The total disappearance of these glaciers will trigger significant ecological, economic, and cultural consequences across the region. Unique high-mountain ecosystems will be disrupted as specialized micro-organisms and algae lose their natural habitats.

At the same time, loweraltitude plant and animal species will migrate higher up the slopes, placing severe competitive pressure on the niche environments of summit areas. Economically and visually, East Africa will lose its signature white mountain tops.

While seasonal snow will still fall on the high peaks occasionally, permanent ice caps shining in the distance will be gone, impacting mountain tourism and eliminating rare tropical glacier research sites that exist in only a few other places globally, such as the South American Andes and Indonesia.

Close 

The loss also carries a profound, often overlooked spiritual impact for local communities. For generations, indigenous societies have viewed these icy summits as sacred dwellings for spirits or deities.

The permanent loss of the ice raises deep cultural and spiritual questions about the human disruption of these sacred landscapes. In theory, the retreat process is physically reversible; an estimated 40 per cent increase in annual snowfall could return Mount Kenya's glacier mass to equilibrium.

However, under current global climate trajectories, there is no realistic prospect of saving East Africa's glaciers. Even under wetter future scenarios, atmospheric temperatures will remain too warm for permanent snow to accumulate on the mountain tops, leaving the region set to shed its ancient ice caps for good.

World.title: Jalen Hurts saves Eagles from ugly upset as Philadelphia escapes Titans to remain unbeaten
World.content:
The Philadelphia Eagles moved to 2-0 with a win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon in Nashville.

That's a sentence most football fans expected to read before the game even started. What most probably didn't expect was exactly what it took for the Eagles to go into Nissan Stadium and beat the Titans.

Jalen Hurts connected with Darius Cooper for a 3-yard touchdown with less than 10 seconds remaining to turn a 20-17 Tennessee lead into a 24-20 Philadelphia victory. The Titans, who looked completely lost last week in a 23-10 loss to the New York Jets, had the reigning NFC East champions on the ropes for much of the afternoon.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Philadelphia's problems started immediately. Star running back Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger on the Eagles' first offensive play and spent most of the first half on the sideline. He returned after halftime wearing a neck roll, but finished with just four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That opening possession lasted more than seven minutes and moved deep into Tennessee territory, but it ended in the worst possible way. Hurts tried to find DeVonta Smith in the end zone, but Amani Hooker intercepted the pass and returned it 92 yards to the Philadelphia 10-yard line. Four plays later, Cam Ward scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak to give Tennessee a 7-0 lead.

The Eagles responded with a 2-yard touchdown run from Tank Bigsby and Hurts connected with Smith for a 22-yard touchdown late in the second quarter. But the Titans refused to go away. Joey Slye kicked a 37-yard field goal just as time expired in the first half, cutting Philadelphia's lead to 14-10.

Jake Elliott extended the lead with a 58-yard field goal in the third quarter, but Ward scored his second rushing touchdown of the game to tie the score at 17.

Philadelphia had an opportunity to take control in the fourth quarter, but Hurts threw his second interception with just over six minutes remaining. The Titans responded with a 69-yard drive that included a 41-yard completion from Ward to Elic Ayomanor and a 27-yard run by Tyjae Spears on third-and-22.

The Eagles' defense eventually held Tennessee to a 33-yard field goal, but that still gave the Titans a three-point lead with 1:56 remaining and Philadelphia had no timeouts.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

That's when Hurts finally looked like the quarterback who led the Eagles to a Super Bowl victory in February 2025.

The 28-year-old signal-caller converted a third-and-6 with a 20-yard completion to Dontayvion Wicks and connected with Smith three times for 34 yards on the drive. Smith's final catch was a sweet grab along the sideline where he barely got his second foot down inbounds. The crucial play went for 19 yards and set the Eagles up at the Tennessee 3-yard line with 20 seconds remaining.

Two plays later, Hurts found Cooper for the game-winning touchdown, the first touchdown catch of Cooper’s NFL career.

Hurts finished 26-of-37 for 264 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Smith caught 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown, accounting for nearly half of Philadelphia's passing production. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Smith has to step up as the team's top receiver, and he looked the part against Tennessee.

AJ BROWN SAYS THERE'S BEEN SILENCE BETWEEN HIM AND EX-TEAMMATE JALEN HURTS SINCE HIS MOVE TO NEW ENGLAND

Ward completed 13-of-20 passes for 183 yards and didn't turn the ball over, while adding both of Tennessee's touchdowns on the ground. It wasn't an especially good performance for the Titans offense, as the Eagles outgained Tennessee 341-291 and out-possessed the Titans by nearly 13 minutes.

The problem for Hurts and the Eagles was the two turnovers and general sloppy play at key moments.

Obviously, it’s hard to panic about a team that won its first two games. But if I were an Eagles fan, I’d feel about as nervous as possible for someone whose team is 2-0.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Philadelphia has beaten Washington and Tennessee by a combined six points. The Commanders might be better than people expected, but the Titans entered Sunday looking like one of the worst teams in football. The Eagles needed a touchdown with nine seconds remaining to beat them.

Good teams find ways to win close games, and Hurts deserves credit for helping the team survive back-to-back upset bids. But a supposed NFC contender cannot continue playing like this and expect to keep escaping.

The standings say the Eagles are perfect. Their play on the field has been anything but.

World.title: McDonald’s once sold beloved cookies featuring forgotten characters from the chain's past
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Introduced in 1974, McDonaldland Cookies became a regular addition to McDonald’s Happy Meals when they debuted nationwide in 1979, but the beloved menu item was discontinued in the early 2000s, to the disappointment of many fans.

The small, crunchy, cookies were baked for McDonald’s by Keebler, had a subtle lemon flavor and featured the faces of beloved McDonald’s characters like Grimace, Ronald McDonald, Birdie, and Hamburglar.

Customers described them as a cross between shortbread and animal crackers, and McDonaldland Cookies came in either a little plastic bag or a brightly colored cardboard box that also showed the faces of McDonald’s characters.

The fast food chain altered its Happy Meals to include healthier items such as apple slices in the early 2000s.

MCDONALD'S REVIVES DECADES-OLD FAVORITE FOR AMERICA 250 AFTER YEARS OF CUSTOMER REQUESTS

Between 2003 and 2004, McDonaldland Cookies were discontinued at all U.S. locations.

Chocolate chip cookies, however, remained on the menu.

McDonald’s has been serving some variation of chocolate chip cookies since the early 1970s, with today's chewy, soft-baked version introduced in 2012.

MCDONALD'S BRINGS BACK POPULAR ITEM FOR SHORT TIME AS ONE STATE GETS A TREAT

Although McDonaldland Cookies are no longer available in the United States, select McDonald’s locations in Australia still offer them, and certain New Zealand restaurants serve the treat under the name "McHappy Cookies."

Fans have also shared on Reddit that a cookie with a flavor and texture similar to the original McDonaldland cookies is available at Aldi supermarkets.

AMERICA'S FAVORITE FAST-FOOD CHAIN NAMED: MCDONALD'S WINS HEARTS BUT NOT BEST BURGER, SURVEY SAYS

One Reddit user commented: "I am eating the Benton's animal crackers from Aldi right now and they taste exactly like the McDonaldland cookies."

McDonaldland Cookies might be gone in the U.S., but the characters have not been totally forgotten.

The viral Grimace Shake, a purple-hued milkshake with a vanilla soft serve base and mixed berry flavoring, came out in 2023 as a limited-time treat to celebrate the beloved character’s birthday.

Beginning in 2022, McDonald's sporadically released various limited-edition Adult Happy Meals, allowing grownups to enjoy the nostalgia of Happy Meals — which, depending on their age, might have included McDonaldland Cookies.

World.title: Keenan Allen faces NFL suspension after blood alcohol level nearly triple the legal limit: report
World.content:
The NFL could be dishing out a suspension to Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen after he was charged this week with two misdemeanors stemming from his arrest on charges of drunk driving before the start of the season.

Allen is facing preliminary charges of operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated (OVWI) as well as OVWI endangering a person, which are both misdemeanors in Indiana.

However, Allen had a blood alcohol level of .224 when he was arrested, which is almost triple the legal limit of .08, per Yahoo Sports. The high BAC is a higher Class A misdemeanor in Indiana.

World.title: Massage clients report bizarre flu-like reaction after popular spa treatment
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A popular wellness treatment is allegedly leaving some people with unexpected symptoms, including aches, fatigue and headaches.

Social media users have described feeling under the weather after getting a massage, with some saying they feel as though they are coming down with an illness.

The reaction is sometimes referred to online as "massage flu," though health experts say it is not an actual medical diagnosis.

DO RED LIGHT THERAPY AND COLD PLUNGES REALLY WORK? A DOCTOR REVEALS THE TRUTH

"This phenomenon is something I have definitely heard of and had patients tell me," W. Zach Smith, a Seattle-based physical therapist and co-founder of HIDEF Physical Therapy, told Fox News Digital.

"The idea of this has been around a long time but usually described as fatigue and soreness," Smith said. "The flu part of the name I have heard more recently."

Soreness can happen when a lot of pressure is applied to the muscles for a long period of time, especially if someone is not used to getting massages, Smith added.

"Any time you go in and apply a lot of pressure to a muscle for a long period of time, it can essentially bruise the tissue," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The body may also have a mild inflammatory response after a massage, which can contribute to soreness, Smith said.

Drew Voelsch, a chiropractor at Forza Chiropractic in Illinois, said he has also heard patients refer to the reaction as "massage flu" or an "adjustment hangover."

"The symptoms are real," Voelsch told Fox News Digital, pointing to soreness, fatigue and mild headaches that may last 24 to 48 hours. "The label is social media."

A massage around the neck, scalp or jaw can also trigger headaches because those areas can be involved in tension headaches, according to Smith.

CLICK HERE TO 

Both experts pushed back on the idea that these symptoms are caused by a massage "releasing toxins" from the body, a claim that has circulated in social media comments.

"This is a myth," Smith said. "There is no basis or science behind this."

Voelsch agreed, noting that the liver and kidneys handle the body's waste-removal processes.

To help reduce discomfort, Smith recommended asking for less pressure or a shorter massage and gradually working up to deeper or longer sessions.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Voelsch also suggested drinking water, eating something light beforehand and moving gently afterward.

Mild soreness is typically not a cause for concern, but Smith said new or persistent pain may be a reason to contact a doctor.

"If you are having a new, unexplained pain that is persistent, that would be a good time to call your doctor," he said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Voelsch recommended seeking medical advice if symptoms last longer than about 72 hours or include fever, sharp or radiating pain, numbness or tingling, spreading swelling or bruising, or faintness.

World.title: ICE shooting rocks Austin as Democrat demands bodycam video, independent probe
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

An angry crowd erupted in yelling, whistles and obscenities near the scene of an ICE-involved shooting that left an adult man seriously wounded on an Austin street Sunday.

Video from the scene showed people holding up their phones and carrying flags as the commotion unfolded. Police said preliminary information indicated the man was shot once in the torso during a brief foot pursuit involving ICE. He remained hospitalized in serious but stable condition.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis and Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz confirmed ICE was involved in the shooting and provided what they repeatedly stressed were preliminary details during a Sunday afternoon news conference.

Austin-Travis County EMS was notified of the shooting at approximately 12:56 p.m. and arrived in less than five minutes, Luckritz said. The adult man was taken from the scene within nine minutes and transported to a local trauma center in serious but stable condition after being shot once in the torso.

Davis said preliminary information indicated there was a brief foot pursuit before the shooting, but cautioned that she had not yet been briefed by federal authorities.

'SQUAD' MEMBER CALLS DHS 'GREATEST THREAT TO OUR SAFETY' AFTER ICE-INVOLVED SHOOTING

"From what I'm hearing, there was a small foot pursuit," Davis said. "But again, this is all very preliminary."

Watson stressed that the information available was "extremely preliminary." He said city officials wanted to make themselves available as quickly as possible when they had information, but warned against rushing to conclusions based on early claims circulating on TikTok, X and other social media platforms.

Watson added that the Austin Police Department was not involved in the shooting and only assisted with traffic control. APD's Special Investigations Unit and the Texas Rangers will work together to investigate the incident, Davis said.

"The city of Austin deserves answers," Davis said. "We're going to get all those questions answered, and we'll be as transparent as we can be."

Watson said he was "very angry" and "extremely unhappy" about the shooting, while accusing ICE of creating fear and chaos in Austin and other cities. He also questioned the agency's ability to investigate itself without local involvement.

ICE AGENTS IN FATAL HOUSTON SHOOTING WERE NOT WEARING BODY CAMERAS, SOURCES SAY

Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, claimed in a post on X that "ICE has shot a person in Austin this morning" and called for a full, independent investigation and the immediate release of body-camera footage.

"Over and over, ICE has shot people and then lied about what happened," Casar wrote. "We will demand truth, transparency and accountability."

During the news conference, Casar called the incident part of a "disturbing pattern" and said ICE's conduct "has got to stop."

"They've arrested 5-year-olds ... and now someone has been shot," Casar said. "This has got to stop."

Authorities have not identified the man who was shot or fully disclosed what led to the encounter.

The Austin investigation comes amid heightened tensions over federal immigration enforcement operations across the country.

ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS CLASH WITH AGENTS OUTSIDE NEW JERSEY DETENTION CENTER AS GOV SHERRILL DENIED ENTRY

Clashes erupted outside New Jersey's Delaney Hall immigration detention center in May after protesters defied a state police order to move to a designated demonstration area. Newark Mayor Ras Baraka later criticized the tactics used by state troopers sent to secure the facility, which had become the focus of frequent demonstrations.

Federal immigration operations also drew national scrutiny in Minnesota following the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. Good was killed by an ICE agent in early January after authorities said she tried to use her vehicle to run over federal officers, while Pretti was fatally shot by agents on Jan. 24 as he recorded federal officers.

Fox News Digital reached out to ICE and the Texas Department of Public Safety for additional information and comment.

World.title: Trump, Iranian president converge on NYC for ‘dramatic’ UN showdown as Tehran faces tight restrictions
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are set to converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly (UNGA) this week, setting up what former White House officials describe as a "dramatic" diplomatic moment, with Tehran’s delegation effectively "captive" under U.S. restrictions amid heightened Middle East tensions.

Pezeshkian, for one, is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday, Reuters and Iran's semi-official news agency, Mehr, reported Sunday, with Trump at the rostrum on Tuesday.

"The choreography here is going to make for a fairly dramatic moment," Theo Wold, former acting assistant attorney general and White House domestic policy advisor, told Fox News Digital.

PUTIN, XI AND IRAN'S PEZESHKIAN DESCEND ON INDIA FOR HIGH-STAKES BRICS SUMMIT AMID ESCALATING GLOBAL TENSIONS

"For the Iranians, the limitation is going to be that there's going to be less access to the international press and less ability for them to essentially poke the Trump administration in the eye," Wold added before noting that it is "pretty sensible to allow them to participate in the international forum and to discuss whatever issues they think are pertinent to their regime and then tell them to go home."

The high-profile gathering also comes as Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran amid the almost seven-month war. Tehran, meanwhile, has set seven conditions for talks with Washington, according to Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei.

Iran also warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, Reuters reported.

While the U.S. approved visas for Iran’s delegation earlier this week, including Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the State Department has placed strict limits on Iranian movements while in Manhattan.

As the host country under a 1947 U.N. agreement, the United States generally must facilitate the entry and transit of foreign representatives traveling to U.N. headquarters, including officials from adversarial nations.

"While ordinary Iranians endure brutal repression, water and electricity shortages, and soaring inflation, the regime's officials want to go on shopping sprees in New York. Not on our watch," U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X.

UN WATCHDOG SLAMS POTENTIAL ELECTION OF IRAN TO PANEL WITH HUMAN RIGHTS SWAY: 'LUNATICS RUNNING THE ASYLUM'

For Washington, Wold said the U.S. is not obligated to give them unrestricted access beyond diplomatic responsibilities.

"Here, the delegation will be restricted to their accommodation in New York City and the U.N. headquarters there in Manhattan," Wold clarified.

He characterized the move by Washington as a way of telling the delegation it could participate in official discussions but not "go and buy a bunch of microwaves or a small car at Costco or a dealership in the greater New York area."

"Some of the restrictions fully recognize that when Iran comes to New York for UNGA, really it's about them lining their pockets and going on shopping sprees to get household appliances and Rolex watches," Wold said. "They're not going to be going on shopping sprees. They're certainly not going to be hitting up Michelin-starred restaurants in greater Manhattan.

"They also go to Sam’s Club and Walmart and Costco. And that was one of the specific prohibitions issued by the State Department this week: to contact those big-box retailers that require a basic membership and say, ‘You’re not to transact or do any business with Iranians when they arrive, and you’re to notify us when they do.’"

KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL

Despite the restrictions, Wold said UNGA gives Washington the opportunity it has "wanted for quite some time to have a large enough audience, and a sort of captive Iranian delegation" to make some of the essential points for why the administration pursued the actions it did against the Iranian regime.

Iranian state media also reported Sept. 19 that Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said New York held "absolutely no charm" for the Iranian delegation.

Baghaei, Mehr News Agency reported, went on to accuse the U.S. of using every tool to block the delegation’s participation, asserting that Iran’s attendance is a legal right rather than a favor.

Wold went on to criticize the U.N. for hosting state representatives hostile to American interests while raising security concerns.

"It's going to be one of those things that's fairly perplexing to most Americans," Wold said. "How is it that the representatives of what we have long identified as a hostile regime, but now one that we're actually engaged in combat operations against, one that has killed American service members, why is it that their diplomats get to come to the United Nations and exchange niceties with other kleptocrats or some of their other allies on the international scene?"

TWO US SERVICE MEMBERS KILLED IN IRANIAN STRIKES ON JORDAN, CENTCOM SAYS

Wold also added that the United Nations wants to "lecture us about international climate change or the need to trans children, but the other is happy to sort of serve as a forum for obvious violators of human rights and obvious regimes that are contrary to any number of internationally agreed-upon protocols."

Amid the hostility between Washington and Tehran, Wold said the gathering could also provide an opening for diplomacy. Trump is also slated to hold bilateral and sideline meetings with leaders from the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to discuss regional security and the Strait of Hormuz.

"There's the hope that there'll be an opportunity for real discussion," Wold said of UNGA. "Everyone's hope, especially from State Department leadership, is that there'll be an opportunity to have a fulsome, sort of meaningful discussion with the Iranians, freed from some of the theatrics the Iranians have engaged in.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"There's a hope that there'll be an opportunity for closed-door private discussions between the United States and Iranians and really try to hammer out some kind of agreement about what a cessation of hostilities will look like."

Wold expressed confidence in Washington’s posture heading into the summit.

"The president is best equipped for these moments. This is really where he sort of shines as a natural leader," he said. "He's not one to bend or to break. It's a precarious time for President Trump, but I have no doubt at all that he'll rise to the moment."

World.title: ICE officer shoots man in Austin, Texas, officials say
World.content:
One person has been hospitalized after an ICE agent-involved shooting occurred in Austin, Texas, on Sunday afternoon, officials said.

The victim, who was identified as a man, was transported to a local hospital and is in “in serious but stable condition” after being shot in the torso, Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz said at a news conference.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson said the Austin Police Department was not involved in the incident.

It was not immediately clear what the victim’s nationality is and whether he was a target of an ICE operation. Those questions “still need to be answered,” Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis said.

The shooting occurred around 1 p.m. Davis said investigators are on scene and she is in contact with Homeland Security Investigations and other state law enforcement agencies.

“A person being shot on the streets of Austin by someone purporting to be law enforcement, particularly when it’s ICE, is something that causes me to be unhappy and angry,” Watson said at the news conference. “While I’m unhappy and I’m angry about it, I’m not surprised at all.”

People gathered across the street from the scene of the shooting Sunday. NBC News

U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, said he is demanding an independent investigation, the release of body camera footage and “accountability for any ICE officer who broke the law.”

“Over and over, ICE has shot people and then lied about what happened. We can see the lies with our own eyes. We will demand truth, transparency and accountability,” he said in a post on X.

Watson said he has asked for the city of Austin to be involved in any forthcoming investigations.

NBC News has reached out to the Department of Homeland Security and the White House for comment.

In July, an ICE officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican national, in Houston during an attempted traffic stop to conduct an immigration arrest.

World.title: Trump says his proposed arch will include a military complex housing drones and snipers
World.content:
President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post Sunday that he would convert plans for a Washington, D.C.-area “Triumphal Arch” to those for “a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch” at the request of the U.S. military, citing “national security.”

The new plan, he said, is to “house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage.”

Reached for comment, a Pentagon spokesperson said the department has “nothing additional to provide beyond the post.” The White House declined to provide additional information.

His post marked a significant change in plans that had already been in progress, as the Trump administration had announced earlier this month that it was preparing to break ground in the coming weeks.

A model of President Trump's planned "Triumphal Arch" at the Great American State Fair in Washington, D.C., on July 2. Joe Raedle / Getty Images file

The president’s announcement was also the second time he has framed a controversial construction project as a national security endeavor. Trump previously argued that the White House ballroom construction was necessary for national security and tied the project to an underground military complex.

The ballroom, too, has faced legal pushback, though the Supreme Court ruled at the end of August that the administration could move forward on ballroom construction indefinitely. The National Trust for Historic Preservation sued over the ballroom, arguing that Trump did not have the unilateral ability to undertake the project. The Supreme Court, though, ruled that the trust likely did not have proper standing to bring the case forward.

In early April, the White House argued to a federal appeals court that the project, including the ballroom, was “necessary to ensure the safety and security of the White House and its grounds.” Weeks later, a gunman stormed a security checkpoint at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, prompting the president to issue renewed calls for a White House event space. The annual dinner is hosted by the White House Correspondents’ Association, not the White House.

Artist renderings and diagrams of the new White House East Wing and ballroom, briefly posted on the National Capital Planning Commission's website, on Feb. 17. Jon Elswick / AP

The proposed 250-foot arch project, which would sit in a roundabout between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, has faced legal challenges from veterans and historians. The project area sits on the Potomac, across from Washington.

The arch proposal has already passed key hurdles, though it’s unclear how Trump’s announcement could affect the prior approvals. In April, the project obtained approval from the Commission of Fine Arts, which is now composed of the president’s allies after he fired previous members. In July, the National Capital Planning Commission, which is led by Trump appointees, approved the preliminary site and building plans. The arch, which would sit a few miles from Reagan airport, also passed the Federal Aviation Administration’s air safety standards last week, with the administration announcing that it “would not pose a hazard to aircraft.”

Rep. Don Beyer, D-Va., whose district includes Arlington National Cemetery and is adjacent to the proposed site, slammed Trump’s plan in a post to X.

“Putting a drone launching site directly in the landing path for DCA is a stupid, dangerous, and unworkable idea,” he said in the post.

The project appeared poised to move forward imminently. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum announced on Sept. 3 that the administration was preparing to start excavation work “over the next two-week period.” U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered the Trump administration to provide 48 hours’ notice before it starts “any activity” on the arch, other than work to determine whether there are archaeological resources on the proposed site.

Trump has made Washington-area construction projects a key priority during his second term. Besides plans for the ballroom and arch, the president also moved to renovate the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, added a White House helipad and pushed to fix fountains in the capital.

Following the renovation of the Reflecting Pool, chunks of the pool’s new coating floated to the surface and the water turned green with algae. Trump also repeatedly claimed, without evidence, that vandalism led to the damage.

World.title: Ed Sheeran calls situation in Gaza ‘unjustifiable’ in first concert since Macklemore controversy
World.content:
Demonstrators shouted “Free, free Palestine” in unison as motorists honked their horns in support.

Robert Boucher, 73, a retired surgeon, said he was there to take a stand for freedom of speech.

“The action that’s been taken by the stadium owners and folks who oppose Macklemore and what he represents and the comments that he’s made, that’s really an unjustifiable attempt to squelch free speech,” Boucher said.

The Philadelphia resident asserted that his criticism is of the Israeli government and its treatment of civilians in Gaza, not a stance against Jewish people.

“We’re here to specifically support our right to say the things that we’re saying and to not be labeled as antisemites or anti-Israel,” he said.

Gwen Myrick, 51, of West Philadelphia, said she supports Macklemore’s stand.

“I am here in support of Macklemore,” she said. “Because that is how a movement is born — standing up for the people who are brave enough to stand up.”

Robert Boucher, a retired surgeon, asserted that criticism of the state of Israel for its treatment of civilians in Gaza is not a stance against Jewish people. Nicole Acevedo / NBC News

The protest followed a weeklong controversy that began after Macklemore voiced support for Palestinians. He accused Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, of organizing a boycott among stadium owners in response, an allegation Kraft did not deny.

In a statement, Kraft, a staunch supporter of Israel and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, said the decision was not intended to stifle Palestinian advocacy or diminish Palestinian suffering but to ensure a “welcoming environment” at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. Macklemore had been scheduled to open two “Loop” tour dates there later this month.

Sheeran said previously that the company promoting his tour made the final decision to drop Macklemore because it held the rapper’s contract.

Messina Touring Group did not respond to multiple requests for comment from NBC News. The promoter told Rolling Stone that it had been informed that multiple venues “will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup,” resulting in his removal.

Macklemore had been scheduled to open Saturday’s show in Philadelphia. Instead, the protesters outside Lincoln Financial Field repeated some of the same pro-Palestinian remarks that Macklemore said led to his removal.

Adi Chattopadhyay, who said he helped organize the demonstration, said Sheeran could halt criticism by donating money to Palestinian-related causes.

“Send that money to families in Gaza,” he said. “Will he support the innocent people of Gaza who have been bombarded? Will he actually do something?”

Macklemore has pledged to donate $1 million, which he said represented all of the net earnings from Sheeran’s tour, to six organizations supporting Palestinians. Kraft later pledged $2 million toward causes supporting people impacted by the war in Gaza to match a similar donation made by Sheeran.

On Saturday, Sheeran told fans at his show that he’s spoken to “people across the spectrum to work out how to make a contribution that helps victims of these terrible times.”

Sheeran, right, said previously that the company promoting his tour made the final decision to drop Macklemore, left, because it held the rapper’s contract. Getty Images

‘I just really came for Ed Sheeran’

Despite the controversy, fans inside the stadium said they were excited to watch Sheeran’s performance, and weren’t bothered by the lack of opening acts.

Friends Karen Mossop, 59, and Karen Macort, 62, said they were there to experience only one artist — Sheeran.

Mossop defended Sheeran and said he just “got caught up in a really negative campaign.”

“Because he’s a really nice guy, he didn’t realize the ramifications of what would happen,” she said.

Mossop also questioned the professionalism of the artists who dropped out.

“It’s a shame that the opening acts quit,” she said. “They’re supposed to be professionals, and they should have acted professionally.”

Alexandria Rasa, 27, of neighboring New Jersey, said she was excited to experience her second Sheeran concert.

“I just really came for Ed Sheeran,” Rasa said. “I don’t really care about his opening acts, so that didn’t really affect me.”

Friend Hannah Luster, 26, also of New Jersey, was focused on the task at hand — basking in the music.

“[I’m] definitely going to enjoy it, probably going to take a video or two,” she said.

Fans inside the stadium said they were excited to watch Sheeran’s performance and weren’t bothered by the lack of an opening act. Heather Barry / Getty Images

Dale Dietrich, 46, and his friend, Jeanine Fusik, 47, were hoping that Taylor Swift, who has been known to join Sheeran onstage, and vice versa, might appear with him Saturday night.

“Ed needs to be rescued,” Dietrich said, referring to fallout from Macklemore’s departure, “and there’s probably one person that can really do it.”

Sheeran did not appear to need saving once the show got underway, though. But he did address the absence of his normal “B stage,” saying it was missing “because I was afraid of what might happen if I stood in the middle, and I will admit that.”

Sheeran spent much of his time onstage as a one-man band — a style fans will recognize from past performances — letting his vocals, instruments and loop pedal command the stadium crowd. But he also got some backup after calling a friend for last-minute help.

The fill-in musicians — a drummer, keyboardist, bassist, guitarist and violinist — had three days to learn the songs, Sheeran said, and he thanked them for their support.

He seemed most grateful to the audience at Lincoln Financial Field.

“Today has honestly been the best show of my life” he said. “I’ve felt so much love from you guys, and I am so grateful.”

The concert ended with fireworks and a crowd on its feet.

Nicole Acevedo reported from Philadelphia, and Dennis Romero from San Diego.

World.title: American dream of owning a home out of reach for many as mortgage rates soar (again)
World.content:
The average interest rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage soared to 7.2% this week, its highest in a year and a half. Coupled with home prices near record highs, it’s putting the American dream of owning a home further out of reach for millions.

“We don’t want to buy this big, beautiful house only to just sit in it, staring at each other, stressing about a mortgage payment every month,” said Alexandra DeCandia, who teaches biology at Georgetown University.

DeCandia and her husband, Edward Schrom, both 33, are looking for their first home in the Washington area. They hope to start a family and want to buy a home before they do.

“It’s something that’s a huge decision and one that will impact us, as well as our future family,” DeCandia said. “It’s very stressful to try to figure that out in this shifting landscape.”

Mortgage rates were on a downswing earlier this year, hitting 5.99% in late February. But ever since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28, they have skyrocketed.

Mortgage interest rates are heavily influenced by the yield on 10-year Treasury bonds, which has been rising as oil prices soar and drive up the cost of goods across the economy.

And mortgage rates could keep rising. The Federal Reserve this week hiked its key interest rate in an effort to get a handle on inflation — and it suggested it may raise rates again this year. Higher rates can drive up borrowing costs across the economy.

Meanwhile, the average home price nationwide is near a record high, at $429,100 as of August.

One bright spot for homebuyers, however, is inventory. There were 1.62 million unsold homes on the market in August, according to the National Association of Realtors.

That’s equal to 4.9 months’ supply, which is measured as the time it would take at the current pace of sales to sell all those homes. That is the highest level in more than a decade, and it gives prospective homebuyers more room to negotiate prices.
